HOW TO USE
THE EMERGENCY
OXYGEN MASK
1. WHERE TO LOCATE MASKS.
The oxygen masks are located in the center seat
back of three place seats, and in the aisle seat back
of the two place seats. In the forward and aft
lounge, masks are located overhead, or on
adjacent bulkheads.
These masks will be automatically released to you
whenever oxygen is required.
Jet flights are conducted above 25,000 ft. with the cabin pressurized
to an altitude of 5,000 to 8,000 ft. If the cabin pressure is lost,
you are at the same altitude as the aircraft, and it is imperative
that you immediately put on the oxygen mask as indicated below.
2. HOW TO USE. Take nearest mask firmly in
hand and pull it from its holder. As mask is
removed, a cord connecting it to the compartment
"must be pulled free." This allows oxygen to flow.
3. UNCOIL OXYGEN TUBE AND PLASTIC
BAG. The coiled oxygen tube, plastic bag, and
head band are stored inside the mask and should
be lifted out. The oxygen supply tube is long
enough that you may relax comfortably in your seat
after mask is on your face.
4. PLACE MASK OVER NOSE AND MOUTH.
Slip head band over head and adjust to fit. Do not
overtighten head band as this may misshape mask
and cause discomfort.

FOR YOUR SAFETY. Know how to move
DC-8 DOMESTIC
JET MAINLINER
out of this airplane fast. There is fire-danger
any time a landing is other than normal-par-
ticularly when the airplane structure is damaged.
Below is a floor plan of the plane you are in. Familiarize yourself with the location of the
exits. Note particularly the exits nearest you. Study how they are opened and also the
protective position you should assume during an emergency landing. When leaving,
move to the exits immediately. Do not go back for coats, purses, or other personal items.
A WORD ABOUT YOUR SEAT BELT-Rough air (turbulence) at high altitudes,
although infrequent, can be severe. When the seat belt sign is lighted in-flight, please
comply with the sign to prevent possible injury. Seasoned air travelers usually leave their
seat belts fastened all the time and pull them up snug whenever the seat belt sign is lighted.
Occasionally, because of schedule patterns, DC-8 aircraft equipped with ocean
ditching equipment also operate within the continental United States.
